nota: Offshore wind milestone calendar for the North Sea and the Baltic (GB, NL, BE, DE, DK, NO, SE, FI, PL, LT, LV, EE, FR, EU), 2023-2027 with later anchors. Curated items with source, link and source date; null = not found, never estimated. 'status' is curated (done/scheduled/at risk); 'status_effective' adds 'unconfirmed' when a scheduled date has passed without confirmation. Reliability high/medium/low = alta/media/bassa. 'precision' tells how exact the date is. 'candidati_rss' are suggestions from the offshoreWIND.biz feed, NOT verified items.

awarded_vs_targets.nota: Supported or zero-subsidy capacity awarded in auctions/tenders (status done), by year of award. Site-right auctions without revenue support (e.g. Estonia Saare 1) are not counted. Gap = target minus installed end-2025 (WindEurope national totals via eolico-filiera.json; include seas outside North Sea/Baltic for GB, FR, DE, DK). Awarded capacity mostly comes online after 2030: the share is an upper bound for target delivery.

per_country.target_note: Ostend Declaration (about 6 GW around 2030, 8 GW 2040); Princess Elisabeth Zone first phase now tied to energy island deadline of 1 Oct 2031.
WindSeeG: 30 GW 2030, 70 GW 2045 (confirmed in the August 2026 reform draft).
Secondary source (Port Esbjerg); Denmark itself now plans commissioning of the 2026 awards in 2032.
National figure (all French seas, mostly Channel/Atlantic); PPE3: 15-18 GW 2035, 45 GW 2050.
Clean Power 2030 Action Plan: 43-50 GW offshore wind by 2030 (whole UK, includes Irish Sea and Celtic Sea).
21 GW moved from 2030 to end-2032 (2024); 2040 goal cut from 50 GW to 30-40 GW (July 2025). The letter to Parliament of 16 March 2026 still says 'approximately 21 GW ... around 2030'.
Ostend Declaration figure; areas for 30 GW to be awarded by 2040.
Polish share quoted in the Marienborg Declaration.

elementi.summary: Context item (before 2023): awarded by lottery among zero-price bids; under construction in 2026.

elementi.price: EUR 12.6 bn in total payments to the state
elementi.summary: Record negative-bidding auction; payments by developers later blamed for weak project economics.
Vattenfall stopped Norfolk Boreas despite an AR4 CfD, citing costs up to 40% higher and a SEK 5.5 bn earnings impact. Marker of the 2023 cost shock.
elementi.source: offshoreWIND.biz (RWE purchase article recalling the stop)

elementi.project: Pre-investigated sites N-3.5, N-3.6, N-6.6, N-6.7
elementi.outcome: N-3.5 and N-3.6 (900 MW) Nordseecluster B (RWE); N-6.6 (630 MW) RWE (Vattenfall step-in right); N-6.7 (270 MW) Waterkant Energy
elementi.summary: Commissioning set for 2028 on all four sites.

elementi.price: administrative strike price GBP 44/MWh (2012 prices) judged too low after cost inflation
elementi.summary: AR5 awarded no offshore wind capacity: developers did not bid because the ceiling price did not cover higher turbine, steel and financing costs. The government raised offshore ceilings by about two thirds for AR6.
First power from the world's largest offshore wind farm under construction (GE Haliade-X 13 MW).

elementi.project: Norfolk zone (Vanguard East, Vanguard West, Boreas)
elementi.summary: RWE agreed to buy Vattenfall's 4.2 GW Norfolk portfolio (GBP 963 m enterprise value; closed March 2024) and restart Boreas. Vanguard East and West won AR7 CfDs in January 2026.
Tender did not go ahead in 2024; Parliament approved new terms in May 2025.

elementi.outcome: awarded to Ventyr (Parkwind/JERA Nex bp and Ingka)
elementi.summary: Norway's first offshore wind auction.

elementi.price: about EUR 3.0 bn in total (EUR 1.305 m/MW and EUR 1.065 m/MW)
elementi.summary: Zero-cent bids triggered dynamic bidding again; RWE left its consortium with TotalEnergies.
elementi.note: Site numbers differ between summaries; not repeated here.

elementi.scheme: zero-subsidy permit, comparative assessment (85% qualitative criteria)
elementi.outcome: Alpha: Noordzeker (SSE Renewables, ABP, AIP); Beta: Zeevonk II (Vattenfall, CIP)
elementi.summary: Largest Dutch tender to date; commissioning originally foreseen end-2029/early-2030.
Artificial island postponed again (to 2036) over costs above DKK 200 bn; tender suspended, a platform-based hub is studied instead.

elementi.outcome: RWE (two sites) and Luxcara (Waterekke Energy, N-9.3)
elementi.summary: Five bids for three sites; total payments not found in the sources checked.
Development paused: no viable investment conditions and no reasonable offshore grid connection; production planned for 2028 abandoned.

elementi.outcome: awarded: Hornsea 4 (2,400 MW) and East Anglia Two phase 1 (963 MW) as new fixed projects; 1,578.5 MW 'permitted reduction' extensions (Hornsea 3 3x360, East Anglia 3B 158.9, Inch Cape 266.1, Moray West 73.5); Green Volt floating 400 MW
elementi.price: GBP 58.87/MWh fixed (2012 prices); GBP 54.23 permitted reduction; GBP 139.93 floating
elementi.summary: Offshore wind back in the UK auction after AR5's failure; Hornsea 4's CfD was later abandoned (May 2025).
Government rejects 13 applications on defence grounds (missile detection); approves Poseidon.

elementi.scheme: two-sided CfD (original design with price cap)
elementi.summary: First tender in the new zone launched, nine months for bids; next two lots 1.4 GW each.

elementi.scheme: no subsidy, state co-ownership and concession payments
elementi.summary: Largest Danish tender ever got no bids; government redesigns with two-sided CfDs.
UK sets a 43-50 GW offshore wind range for 2030 (from about 15 GW then operating); grid connection queue reform follows.
Planned 1.5 GW CfD tender cancelled.

elementi.project: Utsira Nord floating: project area applications
elementi.summary: Only two applications: Harald Harfagre (Deep Wind Offshore, EDF Renewables) and Equinor/Vargronn.
FID with all major component and vessel contracts signed; 25-year indexed CfD; full commissioning targeted end-2027.

elementi.project: Estonian offshore wind CfD reverse auction (up to EUR 2.6 bn)
elementi.summary: Government drops the EU-approved 20-year two-sided CfD auction; in August 2025 the energy minister confirmed no auction in 2026.
Offshore construction of Poland's first offshore wind farm starts.

FID on Germany's largest offshore wind farm; 112 Vestas V236-15 MW, construction from 2026, first phase operational 2028. Nordlicht II became unconditional in January 2026; Vattenfall bought back BASF's stake.

Orsted discontinued Hornsea 4 'in its current form' despite its AR6 CfD, citing supply chain costs, interest rates and execution risk; break-away costs DKK 3.5-4.5 bn. Seabed rights, grid agreement and consent retained.
Dutch government shelves two of the three 2025 tenders and keeps a single-site auction (Nederwiek I-A).
FID and financial close (over EUR 3 bn of project finance each, EUR 700 m EIB); first power planned 2027, full operation 2028.

elementi.outcome: awarded to TotalEnergies; only two bidders
elementi.summary: First site with mandatory overplanting (up to about 1.2 GW). TotalEnergies then launched a strategic review of its German portfolio citing grid connection delays.
Tender halted: legal uncertainty, unrealistic calendar for the energy island and onshore grid, unclear financial framework.
Minister Hermans: 2040 goal of 50 GW 'not realistic', replaced by 30-40 GW; 21 GW kept but for end-2032 (moved from 2030 in 2024). Reasons: slower electrification, higher capex, slow hydrogen market.

elementi.outcome: failed: zero bids (first time in Germany)
elementi.summary: Full merchant risk plus up-front payments deterred bidders; the next tender for the two sites was postponed to 2027.
Commissioning pushed to 2032 and project split into two phases.

elementi.project: Bornholm Energy Island: converters and cables
elementi.summary: Energinet and 50Hertz sign contracts: Siemens Energy converters, NKT HVDC cable (EUR 650 m).

elementi.outcome: void: one bid, minimum is two
elementi.summary: Second failure; government says plans are not abandoned and consults the European Commission.
First Dutch tender without bidders; government switches to subsidised tenders for 2 GW in 2026 and a CfD from 2027.
First of 64 Vestas 15 MW turbines connected to the grid.

elementi.project: CfD tenders: North Sea Mid, Hesselo, North Sea South
elementi.summary: Danish Energy Agency relaunches with state support: net payment caps DKK 15.7 bn (North Sea Mid) and DKK 21.9 bn (Hesselo).
First power after a delay linked to the DolWin5 grid connection (originally slated for Q4 2025 COD).

Commission makes offshore grids a priority, names 'Energy Highways' (including Bornholm Energy Island), faster permitting, and guidance on two-sided CfDs, reported as mandatory for new renewables from 2027 (2029 for offshore hybrids).

elementi.project: First Polish competitive offshore CfD auction
elementi.outcome: Baltica 9 (PGE, 975 MW), Baltic East (Orlen, 900 MW), Baltyk I (Polenergia/Equinor, 1,560 MW)
elementi.summary: Next auctions planned for 2027, 2029 and 2031.

elementi.project: Bornholm offshore wind farms: joint DK-DE tender launch
elementi.summary: In January 2026 the two governments said the joint tender for the wind farms would launch 'in the coming months'. No launch found by November 2026.

elementi.outcome: Oxan Energy (up to 900 MW, about 60 turbines)
elementi.summary: Site rights only, not counted as supported capacity awarded.
SSE project page gives commercial operation in 2026, but turbine installation was still running in November 2026 (vessel Seaway Ventus on site), so slippage into 2027 is likely.
elementi.source: SSE Renewables project page; offshoreWIND.biz (Cadeler, 4 Nov 2026)

elementi.summary: Owners target commercial operation in 2026; no COD date confirmed by November.

elementi.outcome: record 8,245 MW fixed + 192.5 MW floating. North Sea: Dogger Bank South East 1,500 and West 1,500 (RWE), Norfolk Vanguard East 1,545 and West 1,545 (RWE), Berwick Bank B 1,380 (SSE). Irish Sea: Awel y Mor A 775. Floating: Erebus 100, Pentland 92.5
elementi.price: GBP 91.20/MWh England & Wales, GBP 89.49 Scotland, GBP 216.49 floating (2024 prices; 65.45 / 64.23 / 155.37 in 2012 prices)
elementi.summary: Largest offshore wind procurement in a European auction; prices about 19-21% below the administrative ceiling. Most projects deliver phase 1 in 2028/29-2030/31.

elementi.project: Bornholm Energy Island: DK-DE cost-sharing agreement
elementi.summary: Bilateral agreement at the Hamburg summit on cost sharing (support cap up to DKK 139 bn); EUR 645 m CEF grant; 2 GW to Germany, 1.2 GW to Denmark.
300 GW by 2050 confirmed; up to 100 GW cross-border projects (20 GW of cooperation projects for the 2030s); investment pact for 15 GW/year of installations in 2031-2040.

elementi.project: Utsira Nord floating: project areas awarded
elementi.summary: Both applicants each awarded a project area; they now mature projects before licence applications and the aid competition (lowest aid per MW wins; one 500 MW project).
First turbine feeds the Danish grid; 36 of 72 turbines installed by 17 Jul 2026.
Export cable pulled onshore, turbine foundation installation started and first of two offshore converter stations installed; project about 25% complete (from 10% at Q4 2025).
elementi.source: Marine Insight; Orsted Q1 2026 earnings call

elementi.summary: Offshore installation starts (Van Oord, 111 monopiles); all monopiles installed on schedule by August 2026.

elementi.project: North Sea Mid and Hesselo: bid deadline
elementi.summary: Bids received: 2 for North Sea Mid, 5 for Hesselo; the CfD redesign revived competition.
Published in the EU Official Journal; about half floating. Context item: no North Sea sites. Nuclear lobby (FED) seeks suspension; PPE3 appeals pending at the Conseil d'Etat.
All 100 Siemens Gamesa turbines installed on Dogger Bank, 195 km offshore.
Cabinet raises support: maximum tender prices EUR 117/MWh (Gamma-A) and EUR 116/MWh (Gamma-B), up from EUR 104; temporary subsidy mechanism (TOWOZ) before a CfD in 2027.

AR8 opened in July 2026 (brought forward). Offshore administrative strike price frozen at GBP 113/MWh (2024 prices); RenewableUK counts up to 18 offshore wind farms and more than 17 GW eligible; floating gets one extra delivery year.
Developer aim: full operation by end-2026. No first-power announcement found as of 10 Nov 2026, so the year-end target is tight.
RWE schedule: all turbines and the HVDC converter platform commissioned and Sofia fully operational in late 2026.
Energy minister: not feasible on commercial terms without state funding; Ignitis asked to postpone. Positive EIA on 30 Jun 2026; Ignitis buying out Ocean Winds' 49%.

elementi.project: Fyrskeppet (Skyborn) and Vidar (Vattenfall/Zephyr, 2 GW) approved; 11 rejected
elementi.summary: Last EEZ permit decisions: two approved (completion by 2036), 11 rejected on defence grounds. Vattenfall said it would not proceed with Vidar for now; Skyborn says Fyrskeppet needs two-sided CfDs and guarantees.

elementi.project: Swedish state-led tender and support system
elementi.summary: Government commission proposed state-identified sites and support (offshore wind 'not commercially viable' otherwise), with the system taking effect from 1 Jul 2026.
First offshore wind electricity in Poland; Choczewo onshore substation inaugurated the same day; all 76 turbines installed.

elementi.project: Baltic Power export system / Choczewo substation
elementi.summary: Poland's first onshore hub for offshore wind energised; export cables in service.

elementi.project: Princess Elisabeth Zone lot 1: new framework
elementi.summary: New rules: single two-sided CfD, lowest strike price wins, no strike cap, 5-year build window, NZIA criteria (at least 75% of turbines not made or assembled in China, limits on Chinese magnets). Relaunch date not yet published.
First electricity fed into the grid from Nordseecluster A off the German coast.
elementi.note: Capacity 660 MW from RWE project data; check against the release.

elementi.project: Holmsland (ex North Sea I Mid, 1 GW) and Hesselo (0.8 GW)
elementi.price: DKK 504/MWh North Sea Mid (about EUR 68), DKK 542/MWh Hesselo (about EUR 73)
elementi.summary: First successful Danish award since Thor; commissioning targeted for 2032.
elementi.source: Danish Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities

elementi.summary: Aarsleff wins EUR 495 m (DKK 3.7 bn) design-and-build contract for the island's onshore infrastructure.
Draft: annual tenders of 2-4.8 GW from 2027 (replacing fixed 4 GW), two-stage design (dynamic bidding without cap, two-sided CfD only as fallback), 35-year operating life, 70 GW by 2045 kept.
Licence application deadline extended by 12 months while an alternative grid route (via Lista) is reviewed.

Commercial operation (83 x 11 MW); planned for Q1 2026, slipped about five months. Orsted's German fleet now about 2.5 GW. In May 2026 Orsted had cited weather and unplanned TSO grid outages and moved full commissioning to Q3 2026.
Gamma-A was first planned to open for applications in September 2026 (single-site tender); it was merged with Gamma-B into one window opening 26 Nov 2026.

elementi.project: OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII; RWE, TotalEnergies)
elementi.summary: First of 53 monopiles installed; inter-array cables from end-2026, turbines in 2027, full commissioning expected early 2028.

Cabinet sends the bill to the Bundestag (Drucksache 21/8238, 28 Sep 2026) for entry into force on 1 Jan 2027. Offshore Wind Foundation: 16 GW already awarded still lack FID and the bill offers no return-and-retender option.
EIB lends EUR 100 m of a EUR 201 m upgrade for offshore wind logistics; completion now expected end-2027 (earlier source: end-2026).
elementi.source: offshoreWIND.biz, 'EIB backs Lithuanian port's offshore wind upgrade'

elementi.summary: Inaugurated with more than two thirds of turbines connected; all turbines installed by 12 Aug 2026. Original target: fully commissioned by summer 2026.
EnBW expected the full 960 MW for the first time in October 2026.

elementi.project: Gdansk T5 installation terminal (EUR 253 m, 21 ha)
elementi.summary: Terminal serves Baltica 2 turbine installation from Q4 2026 to end-2028.
elementi.source: offshoreWIND.biz (T5 terminal); lease dates from eolico-filiera.json

elementi.summary: 2027 budget: lower penalty for withdrawal before FID, part of the aid paid earlier; NOK 35 bn cap unchanged. Aid competition itself not before about 2028/29 (Equinor).
Bids due; number of bids not published in the sources checked.
Bundesrat rejected the two-stage model in its (non-binding) opinion, siding with industry calls for CfDs as the default.
Nexans starts producing the 525 kV HVDC subsea cables; commissioning expected 2031.
UK's first HVDC subsea cable factory opens; adds cable supply outside the Prysmian/NKT/Nexans backlog.
IFM Investors agrees to acquire 63.9% of ABP, the UK's largest port operator and owner of key east-coast offshore wind bases.
50Hertz awards Fugro the UXO survey and clearance for the LanWin3 grid connection.
elementi.note: An earlier Amprion 'LanWin3' was renamed BalWin2; this is the 50Hertz project named in the RSS item.

elementi.summary: Seaway7 finished inter-array cable lay; first of 95 turbines installed in April 2026, all 95 foundations in place by August.

elementi.project: TenneT 2 GW offshore grid connections (Veerse Meer section)
elementi.summary: DEME and Prysmian start installing TenneT high-voltage cables in the Veerse Meer, part of the Dutch 2 GW programme.
elementi.note: Which wind farm site the section serves is not stated in the RSS summary.

elementi.summary: Turbine installation started off Scotland with Cadeler's new vessel Wind Mover.
elementi.note: Capacity is the project figure commonly quoted (1,080 MW).

elementi.project: Ecowende (Hollandse Kust West VI; Shell, Eneco, Chubu)
elementi.summary: Van Oord and Vestas installed the final turbine; commissioning follows.

elementi.project: Port of Raahe offshore wind logistics
elementi.summary: Port of Raahe and Buss Ports sign an MoU on developing an offshore wind logistics hub; Finland has no state-supported offshore auction.
Cadeler adds the vessel Wind Apex to the Dogger Bank C turbine installation campaign; EMODnet lists completion in 2027.
Vattenfall and the Danish Energy Agency sign final agreements; FID and approvals still pending, commissioning aim 2032.
Marine licence from the MMO for the export cable of Berwick Bank's third phase; phase B (1,380 MW) holds an AR7 CfD and Seaway7 is preferred EPCI for foundations (Oct 2026).

elementi.scheme: subsidised permit (temporary TOWOZ mechanism), price caps EUR 117 / 116 per MWh
elementi.summary: Application window for both 1 GW sites, sharing one TenneT 2 GW platform landing at Maasvlakte. RVO expects the procedure to conclude in December 2026; award date not published. Litmus test after Nederwiek I-A's zero bids.
elementi.source: RVO (Dutch page, Gamma-B); Renewable Energy Industry

elementi.summary: Indicative window: sealed bids between 1-7 Oct and 3-9 Dec 2026, results between 27 Nov 2026 and 17 Feb 2027 depending on qualification appeals, contract signature to early March 2027. Key test of whether AR7 prices hold with a GBP 113 ceiling.
elementi.source: Foot Anstey / law-firm summaries of the AR8 framework
elementi.note: Not checked against the DESNZ allocation framework itself.

elementi.summary: Adoption needed in December for the 1 Jan 2027 start. Trade press conflicts on whether the Bundestag has already voted; no final vote date confirmed.
Ministers expect the first winners at end-2026 / early 2027; the presidential campaign is a political risk.

elementi.project: Curonian Nord: decision on further implementation
elementi.summary: Ignitis says a decision on the project's future (continue, postpone, state support) is due by end-2026.
Retender of the 2025 failed sites postponed to 2027; volume within the 2-4.8 GW annual corridor.
Planned start of the new auction regime; first tenders under it (including the N-10.1/N-10.2 retender) in 2027.

elementi.project: Dunkerque (EDF Renewables, Enbridge, RWE; awarded 2019 at about EUR 44/MWh)
elementi.summary: France's only North Sea project: EDF's 2026 commissioning target is out of date; trackers put operation in 2027-2028 and the project was still pre-construction in February 2026 (substation contract to Chantiers de l'Atlantique, Dec 2024).
elementi.source: Black Ridge Research; Global Energy Monitor

elementi.summary: National Grid's enabling and reinforcement works at Norwich Main substation delay the grid connection by up to two months on the critical path: Orsted now expects first power in Q1 2027 (aim in Nov 2024: commissioning end-2026/H1 2027). Grid, not turbines, is the constraint.
Next auction in the 2027-2029-2031 sequence (Orlen Neptun's Baltic West sites already in wind measurement, Nov 2026).
First power H1 2027, full commercial operation by end-2027 (107 x SG 14-222).

elementi.project: NKT Karlskrona HVDC cable factory expansion
elementi.summary: New capacity enters service in 2027; NKT order backlog EUR 13.0 bn (June 2026).
Remaining 36 turbines by end-2026; testing and full commissioning by spring 2027. Denmark's largest offshore wind farm.

Turbine repairs hold up commissioning: LCCC approved moving the CfD start date of the first 300 MW tranche from 30 Nov 2026 to 31 Jul 2027. Developers still expect the farm 'substantially available' by end-2026. Originally due for commercial operation in 2025.
Full commissioning expected in the six months between Q4 2027 and Q1 2028; world's largest single offshore wind farm when complete.
Bid deadline autumn 2028; at least 1 GW, completion by end-2034.

elementi.project: ELWIND (Latvia-Estonia joint project; LV side up to 1,000 MW)
elementi.summary: Pre-development to 2029, then an auction for the site rights; operation expected 2035. No CfD auction before then.

elementi.project: TenneT IJmuiden Ver Beta 2 GW HVDC (to Maasvlakte)
elementi.summary: Platform steel cut (GE Vernova/Seatrium); TenneT targets commissioning in 2029. RVO roadmap: Alpha Q3 2029, Beta Q4 2029, Nederwiek I Q4 2030, Gamma farms Q2 2032 in RVO's current roadmap (checked 19 Aug 2026; the earlier plan, Gamma Q2 2031, predates the one-year platform delay); Nederwiek II and Gamma platforms already one year late for supply chain reasons.
BalWin1 slips one year from 16 Sep 2030 to 15 Sep 2031 (extra converter platform work, difficult onshore ground); BalWin2 revised date pending. Blocks 2 GW of already awarded turbines for a year.
Royal decree sets 1 Oct 2031 as the deadline for the first phase of the energy island (island itself under construction, about EUR 3.6 bn).
Target year for the hub (originally 2030).
